specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** folio-quarto-octavo-paper-calculator
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Apply
**Bloom Verb:** calculate
**Learning Objective:** The learner will calculate the number of pages and sheets of paper needed for one copy of Virgil's works in folio, quarto, or octavo format at a given number of lines per page, getting all three challenge calculations exactly right within two attempts each. **Prerequisites:** sheet, folio, quarto, octavo, italic type, commentary, Aldine editions (all defined in the section "Aldine Editions" above). **Evidence of Mastery:** For three challenge editions, the learner types the number of pages and the number of sheets per copy before the sim shows the folded sheet. An answer is correct when both numbers equal the model values exactly. Mastery is all three challenges correct within two attempts each. Free exploration with the controls afterward is not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A sheet is a page (a sheet makes 4, 8, or 16 pages). (2) The small format alone explains the Aldine savings, and the compact type and missing commentary did not matter (challenges 2 and 3 show that denser pages halve the paper again). (3) A cheaper book must hold a shorter text (all three challenges print the same 12,900 lines). (4) Pages divide evenly into sheets (a partly used sheet must still be bought, so sheets round up). **Instructional Rationale:** Calculating with a check makes the learner use the fold rule and the rounding rule rather than watch them, which is the Apply-level evidence. Holding the text fixed and changing one variable per challenge lets the learner attribute the savings to the fold and to the page density separately. **Content:** Formats, each with a picture of a sheet folded the stated number of times and its pages numbered: | Format | Folds | Leaves per sheet | Pages per sheet | |---|---|---|---| | Folio | 1 | 2 | 4 | | Quarto | 2 | 4 | 8 | | Octavo | 3 | 8 | 16 | Text: Virgil's *Eclogues*, *Georgics*, and *Aeneid*, 12,900 lines in all (shown as "about 12,900 lines"). Adjustable quantities: | Quantity | Min | Max | Step | Default | Unit | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | Lines of verse per page | 10 | 40 | 5 | 15 | lines | | Copies printed | 100 | 2,000 | 100 | 1,000 | copies | Challenge editions, in this order: | # | Format | Lines per page | Pages | Sheets per copy | Feedback when wrong | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | Folio, verses surrounded by commentary | 15 | 860 | 215 | 12,900 ÷ 15 = 860 pages; a folio sheet makes 4 pages, so 860 ÷ 4 = 215 sheets. | | 2 | Octavo, same 15 lines per page | 15 | 860 | 54 | The same 860 pages, but an octavo sheet makes 16 pages: 860 ÷ 16 = 53.75, and a part-sheet still costs a sheet, so 54. | | 3 | Octavo in compact italic, no commentary | 30 | 430 | 27 | 12,900 ÷ 30 = 430 pages; 430 ÷ 16 = 26.875, rounded up to 27 sheets. | After challenge 3 the sim shows the comparison: folio 215 sheets, octavo 54, Aldine-style octavo 27, so one copy of the Aldine-style octavo uses about one-eighth of the folio's paper; for 1,000 copies, 215,000 sheets against 27,000. **Provenance:** Fold, leaf, and page counts are the standard definitions of the formats (section "Aldine Editions"). The line count is the combined length of Virgil's three works in standard editions, rounded to the nearest hundred. Lines per page are illustrative, not measurements of real editions; the sim labels them "Illustrative page densities." **Rules:** pages = ceiling(12,900 ÷ lines per page). sheets per copy = ceiling(pages ÷ pages per sheet). sheets per edition = sheets per copy × copies. Both ceilings round any fraction up to the next whole number. At 40 lines per page: 323 pages; folio 81, quarto 41, octavo 21 sheets. At 10 lines per page: 1,290 pages; folio 323, quarto 162, octavo 81 sheets. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads challenge 1 (format and lines per page) and types the pages and the sheets per copy. 2. The learner presses Check. The sim folds a sheet into the format, shows the page numbers on its leaves, and shows the model values beside the learner's. 3. The learner repeats for challenges 2 and 3. 4. After challenge 3, free exploration unlocks: the learner chooses any format, lines per page, and copies, and pages, sheets per copy, and sheets per edition update at once. 5. The learner should notice that the fold divides the paper by 4 from folio to octavo, and the denser page halves it again. **Feedback:** Three challenges, fixed order, two attempts each. Correct: "Correct: [pages] pages on [sheets] sheets." Incorrect: the "Feedback when wrong" text for that challenge; if only the sheets are wrong by one, add "Remember to round a part-sheet up." After a second wrong attempt the model values and the worked calculation appear, and the challenge counts as missed. A running count "Challenges correct: n of 3" is shown. After challenge 3: "Same Virgil, about one-eighth of the paper: small fold, dense page." **Starting State:** Challenge 1 with empty answer boxes, an unfolded sheet, and the question "How many sheets of paper does one copy of this Virgil need?" **Chapter Anchors:** About 12,900 lines of Virgil; folio 15 lines per page gives 860 pages and 215 sheets; octavo 30 lines per page gives 430 pages and 27 sheets (430 ÷ 16 = 26.9 rounded up); about one-eighth of the paper; folio 4, quarto 8, octavo 16 pages per sheet.
